metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened woman_sitting_by_the_tree.png in GIMP, applied Brightness-Contrast (-30), then used File > Overwrite to save as PNG.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can use GIMP Colors > Brightness-Contrast and File > Export As (for JPEG export to new filename). Demonstrated saving via File menu.
metadata.explanation: Task requires reducing brightness of the photo and exporting it as 'dark_photo.jpg' on the Desktop via File > Export As. Evaluator checks: dark_photo.jpg exists on Desktop with mean RGB brightness < 68.0 (threshold is ~5% below original mean ~71.74, accepting any genuine brightness reduction). Initial state has no dark_photo.jpg, so initial state fails. [Fixed: removed out-of-scope PNG overwrite check; raised threshold from 65.0 to 68.0 to avoid false negatives for modest reductions; getter simplified to JPEG-only]

scoring_breakdown.jpeg_exported_dark: 1.0 - dark_photo.jpg exists on Desktop with RGB mean brightness < 68.0

fix_history: Fix 1: Removed out-of-scope PNG overwrite check (png_brightness_check) — instruction only requires JPEG export as dark_photo.jpg
Fix 2: Raised brightness_threshold from 65.0 to 68.0 (~5% reduction from original ~71.74) to prevent false negatives for modest but valid brightness reductions
Fix 3: Updated JPEG check to award full 1.0 score instead of 0.5
Fix 4: Simplified getter to JPEG-only; removed png_path from evaluator.result config

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly fetches /home/user/Desktop/dark_photo.jpg from the environment using env.controller.get_file(), checks existence, and computes mean RGB brightness via PIL — directly targeting both instruction requirements.
Metric correctly handles the expected parameter: since expected.type='rule', the framework passes the rules dict directly, so expected.get('brightness_threshold', 68.0) is the correct access pattern.

Coverage is complete: the evaluator checks (a) JPEG file exists at the correct Desktop path named dark_photo.jpg, and (b) mean brightness is below threshold — both requirements from the instruction are covered.

Threshold of 68.0 (~5% below original mean ~71.74) is reasonable: any genuine brightness reduction should produce a mean well below 68.0, minimizing false negatives while still rejecting unmodified exports.

Previous issues (PNG overwrite check out of scope, threshold too strict at 65.0, JPEG scoring only 0.5) have all been fixed per fix_history; the current evaluator awards full 1.0 for JPEG export with reduced brightness.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: JPEG compression can shift RGB mean slightly relative to the original PNG mean (~71.74). If edge cases arise, consider computing threshold dynamically as a fraction of the original image's brightness rather than a fixed value.
validation.fix_notes: PNG overwrite check removed; threshold raised to 68.0 (~5% reduction); JPEG check now awards full 1.0 score
